model: Codex editorial revision of the recorded GPT-5.6 Sol draft

passages.text:
Peter to James, the lord and bishop of the holy church.

May he always be at peace from the Father of all through Jesus Christ. Knowing, my brother, that you eagerly hasten toward what benefits all of us together, I ask and implore you not to share with anyone from the nations the books of my preachings that I sent you, nor with one of our own people before a test. But if someone, after being tested, is found worthy, then make the handover to him according to the procedure by which Moses also made the handover to the seventy who had received his seat. Because of this, the fruit of that safeguarding also remains evident to the present. For their fellow nationals everywhere preserve the same standard of sole sovereignty and communal order, since the writings that point in many directions have in no way been able to lead them off into thinking otherwise. For, according to the standard handed down to them, they try to bring into order what is discordant in the writings, if indeed someone who does not know the traditions happens to grow numb before the many-meaning voices of the prophets. For this reason they permit no one to teach unless that person first learns how the writings must be used. Because of this, among them there is one God, one law, one hope.

lexical_decisions.chosen: May he always be at peace
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the third-person optative of the Greek salutation rather than silently changing it to a second-person form.

lexical_decisions.chosen: not to share with anyone from the nations
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the source’s circumlocution rather than automatically replacing it with the conventional term “Gentiles.”

lexical_decisions.chosen: nor with one of our own people before a test
lexical_decisions.rationale: Ὁμόφυλος denotes someone of the same stock or people, while πεῖρα here denotes testing or trial.

lexical_decisions.chosen: according to the procedure
lexical_decisions.rationale: In this transmission context ἀγωγή refers to the prescribed method or course, without requiring the stronger interpretation “initiation.”

lexical_decisions.chosen: of sole sovereignty and communal order
lexical_decisions.rationale: Represents both abstract nouns while preserving the possible reference to one divine sovereignty and an associated ordered way of communal life.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the writings that point in many directions
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the directional image of νεύω and the plurality expressed by πολλά.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ναρκᾷ πρὸς τὰς τῶν προφητῶν πολυσήμους φωνάς
lexical_decisions.chosen: grow numb before the many-meaning voices of the prophets
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the striking image of becoming numb or benumbed and the semantic multiplicity conveyed by πολυσήμους.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὰ τῶν γραφῶν ἀσύμφωνα πειρῶνται μεταρρυθμίζειν
lexical_decisions.chosen: they try to bring into order what is discordant in the writings
lexical_decisions.rationale: Μεταρρυθμίζειν suggests rearranging or setting right; the rendering does not decide whether the discordance is textual or interpretive.

passages.text: To ensure, then, that the same thing happens among us, give the books of my preachings to our seventy brothers together with the corresponding mystery of the procedure, so that, as for equipping also those who wish to take on a share of the teaching, they may equip them. For if it does not happen this way, our message of truth will be divided into many opinions. I know this not because I am a prophet, but because I already see the beginning of this evil itself. For some of those from the nations rejected the law-conforming proclamation delivered through me and accepted a certain lawless and frivolous teaching of the enemy man. And this while I am still alive: some have attempted, through certain varied interpretations, to reshape my words into the abolition of the law, as though I myself did think in this way but did not proclaim it openly. May that be far away! For such a thing is to oppose the law of God, which was spoken through Moses and attested by our Lord concerning its everlasting continuance. For he said as follows: “Heaven and earth will pass away; one iota or one small stroke will certainly not pass away from the law.” And he said this: “Before all things happen.” But they—I do not know how—while claiming to represent my mind, attempt to interpret the words they heard from me more wisely than I who spoke them, telling those whom they instruct that this is my view—a view I did not even entertain. If they dare to tell such lies about me while I am still alive, how much more, after my time, will those who come after me dare to do this?

lexical_decisions.source_quote: μετὰ τοῦ ὁμοίου τῆς ἀγωγῆς μυστηρίου
lexical_decisions.chosen: together with the corresponding mystery of the procedure
lexical_decisions.rationale: Μυστήριον can denote a secret or restricted matter; “mystery” preserves that ambiguity, while ἀγωγή is rendered consistently as “procedure.”

lexical_decisions.chosen: as for equipping … they may equip them
lexical_decisions.rationale: Uses a topical infinitive followed by a finite verb to preserve both visibly printed forms and their repetition without deleting either one.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὁ τῆς ἀληθείας ἡμῶν διαιρεθήσεται λόγος
lexical_decisions.chosen: our message of truth will be divided
lexical_decisions.rationale: Λόγος here denotes the communicated teaching or message, while the passive image of division is retained.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὸ δι᾽ ἐμοῦ νόμιμον ἀπεδοκίμασαν κήρυγμα
lexical_decisions.chosen: rejected the law-conforming proclamation delivered through me
lexical_decisions.rationale: “Law-conforming” preserves the deliberate contrast between νόμιμον and the following ἄνομόν in a passage about abolishing the law.

lexical_decisions.chosen: of the enemy man
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the definite but unnamed polemical designation without identifying the figure from outside the supplied text.

lexical_decisions.chosen: but did not proclaim it openly
lexical_decisions.rationale: Παρησία here concerns open, forthright public speech rather than merely inward confidence.

lexical_decisions.chosen: concerning its everlasting continuance
lexical_decisions.rationale: The masculine pronoun naturally refers to the law, and διαμονή denotes its continuing or enduring existence.

lexical_decisions.chosen: one iota or one small stroke
lexical_decisions.rationale: Κεραία denotes a small projection or written stroke; the rendering avoids importing a familiar biblical wording.

lexical_decisions.chosen: claiming to represent my mind
lexical_decisions.rationale: The phrase describes professing or claiming access to Peter’s intent, not merely making a promise.

lexical_decisions.chosen: those whom they instruct
lexical_decisions.rationale: Κατηχέω denotes oral instruction here; the accessible wording avoids requiring the later technical sense of “catechumens.”

source_issues.issue: Both verbal forms are confirmed features of the selected print, not an OCR error. Their precise syntactic relationship is uncertain: the infinitive may be topical or resumptive before the finite verb, producing an apparent anacoluthon. No deletion has been adopted. The independent v2 Sol 6.1 review confirms that this disclosure is adequate and that the verified repetition is not an unresolved transcription defect. The interpretation remains provisional, not silently emended.

source_issues.source_quote: μαρτυρηθέντι. περὶ τῆς ἀιδίου αὐτοῦ διαμονῆς.
source_issues.issue: The selected edition’s confirmed full stop leaves the following prepositional phrase syntactically detached. The translation reads it retrospectively with μαρτυρηθέντι; this is an interpretive repunctuation, not a claim of OCR error or a different textual reading.
source_issues.proposed_reading: μαρτυρηθέντι περὶ τῆς ἀιδίου αὐτοῦ διαμονῆς.

passages.text: So that no such thing may happen, it was for this reason that I asked and implored you not to share with anyone the books of my preachings that I sent you, neither with one of our own people nor with one of another people before a test. But if someone, after being tested, is found worthy, then make the handover to him according to Moses’s procedure, by which he made the handover to the seventy who had received his seat. Thus they may guard the pledges and everywhere transmit the standard of truth, interpreting everything in accordance with our tradition; and they may not, while themselves being dragged down through ignorance and drawn into error by speculations within the soul, bring others into the same kind of pit of destruction. And I have set out well for you what seemed good to me; but carry out what seems good to you, my lord, as is fitting. Farewell.

lexical_decisions.chosen: neither with one of our own people nor with one of another people
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the explicit contrast between a person of the same stock and one of a different stock.

lexical_decisions.chosen: according to Moses’s procedure
lexical_decisions.rationale: The context concerns the prescribed manner of restricted transmission, so “procedure” retains the practical force without asserting a specific ritual form.

lexical_decisions.chosen: they may guard the pledges
lexical_decisions.rationale: The plural πίστεις may denote pledges or assurances of fidelity, or beliefs/points of faith. “Pledges” is retained as a provisional contextual interpretation of restricted transmission, not a sense established by the plural alone. “Guard the points of faith” was compared as a main-text alternative; neither sense should be presented as certain, so the alternative is preserved explicitly for readers.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἑρμηνεύοντες τὰ πάντα πρὸς τὴν παράδοσιν ἡμῶν
lexical_decisions.chosen: interpreting everything in accordance with our tradition
lexical_decisions.rationale: Πρός expresses interpretation measured against or oriented toward the received tradition.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὑπὸ τῶν κατὰ τὴν ψυχὴν στοχασμῶν
lexical_decisions.chosen: by speculations within the soul
lexical_decisions.rationale: Στοχασμοί are conjectures or speculative judgments; κατὰ τὴν ψυχήν is retained without reducing it to the more interpretive phrase “personal opinions.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: εἰς τὸν ὅμοιον τῆς ἀπωλείας ἐνέγκωσιν βόθυνον
lexical_decisions.chosen: bring others into the same kind of pit of destruction
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves both the comparison expressed by ὅμοιον and the physical image of a pit in βόθυνον.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὰ μὲν ἐμοὶ δόξαντα καλῶς ἐσήμανά σοι
lexical_decisions.chosen: And I have set out well for you what seemed good to me
lexical_decisions.rationale: The chosen construction attaches καλῶς (“well”) to ἐσήμανα, rather than specifying “clearly.” An alternative attaches καλῶς with δόξαντα, evaluating what seemed good to Peter instead of how he communicated it; on that attachment, “And I have indicated to you what seemed good to me” is an alternative rendering. Both interpretations remain disclosed.

lexical_decisions.chosen: Farewell
lexical_decisions.rationale: This conventional closing literally wishes strength or health but functions as an epistolary farewell.

source_issues.issue: The plural πίστεις may mean pledges/assurances of fidelity or beliefs/points of faith. “Pledges” is a provisional contextual choice, not established by the plural alone.

source_issues.source_quote: τὰ μὲν ἐμοὶ δόξαντα καλῶς ἐσήμανά σοι
source_issues.issue: The English takes καλῶς with the act of setting out (“well”). Alternatively it may qualify what seemed good to Peter; “I have indicated to you what seemed good to me” represents that attachment.

editorial_revision.method: Apply recorded model-review proposals and preserve interpretive alternatives; no new model API generation claimed
